comments.body: Thanks for the review! I have updated the PR according to your comments. All of the descriptions were copied from upstream however I believe that your suggestions are an improvement.

This pull request has been mentioned on **NixOS Discourse**. There might be relevant details there:

https://discourse.nixos.org/t/prs-ready-for-review/3032/6891

Switched back to using preStart and install since tmpfiles wasn't copying new changes when the file already existed. There doesn't seem to be a way to solve this with tmpfiles when reading through tmpfiles.d(5)
Since this service module directly correlates to a package, how about making it a [modular service](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/README-modular-services.md)?
Is there any more information about modular services? I don't really know what needs to be done given the information in the link.

Here is the [Modular Services doc in NixOS Manual](https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/#modular-services).

In short, move the module under the pkgs/by-name/qb/qbit-manage directory as `service.nix` and make it `qbit-manage.passthru.services.default` (considering that there's only one module).

You can search for other such `service.nix` in Nixpkgs.

This pull request has been mentioned on **NixOS Discourse**. There might be relevant details there:

https://discourse.nixos.org/t/prs-already-reviewed/2617/3177

Also please rebase.

I did not read all things again, maybe someone else can give it re-read.

Changed to "Path of the qBittorrent BT_backup directory."

Oh, I get it, you meant the list in the description. I was thinking of a [] list. Fixed.
Maybe an idea to default this to grabbing the address out of `services.qbittorrent`? (Not a blocker on merging in the slightest.)
I don't know how qbit-manage works, but does the config file really go in the data directory, where I presume it also puts various bits of mutable state?
Would there be any benefit to setting `StateDirectory` instead of exposing the `services.qbit-manage.dataDir` setting (and so e.g. getting tmpfiles integration for free)?
Good idea, I have implemented this now
Unfortunately yes, this is where qbit-manage puts all the files that it writes
Good idea, I have switched to this method instead, I see no downsides.

I think it is typically called [`settings`](https://github.com/NixOS/rfcs/blob/master/rfcs/0042-config-option.md).

```suggestion
    settings = mkOption {
```

In addition, you don't have to define each options exhausively.  You could explicitly define entries that
- is referenced elsewhere
- requires special validation
- is very important

and guide users to an upstream manual for the rest of the options.

```suggestion
    concatStringsSep
    getExe
    hasPrefix
    literalExpression
    mkIf
    mkOption
    mkEnableOption
    mkPackageOption
    optional
    optionalString
```
review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,439 @@
+{
+  config,
+  lib,
+  pkgs,
+  ...
+}:
+let
+  cfg = config.services.qbit-manage;
+  yaml = pkgs.formats.yaml { };
+  createYAMLConfig =
+    config:
+    pkgs.runCommand "config.yml" { } ''
+      # Need to run sed to remove the quotes around !ENV values
+      # otherwise qbit-manage will not interpret them as environment variables
+      sed -E "s/'(!ENV) (.*)'/\1 \2/g" '${yaml.generate "tmp" config}' > $out
+    '';
+  inherit (lib)
+    mkIf
+    mkOption
+    mkEnableOption
+    mkPackageOption
+    strings
+    optional
+    optionalString

reviews.body:
Small typo. I don't really have the expertise to review this PR.

I was only curious on how modules were made and found this small typo.

I've looked this over and none of it strikes me as unreasonable, with the caveat that I don't know anything about qbittorrent or qbit-manage. I've got a couple of queries about the best way to do things, but none that should block merging. I assume that the option names are reflecting qbit-manage's and so I'm not going to quibble over the underscores or irregular abbreviations.
